findings.text: _band_limits recomputes the private-shadow height band from a single admitted saddle (lower = upper = saddle_height), while the production helper it is meant to model independently, x_point_height_limits (nova/equilibrium/topology.py:52-66), takes the min and max height over the full admitted X-candidate set to support multi-saddle configurations (snowflake, double-null). Both fixtures used here carry at most one admitted saddle, so the reduction is exact for this oracle and it is not a false pass, but this file alone would not detect a regression in the min/max-over-set behaviour; that behaviour is exercised separately in tests/test_wall_node_private_shadow.py, so overall suite coverage is intact. Non-blocking: worth a one-line docstring note that the helper assumes at most one admitted saddle, so a future reader does not mistake it for a general model of the production rule.

item_verdicts.diff: git show 2bf422abe and f2dcc15cd read commit by commit: one test-only commit (203 lines changed: 68 insertions, 135 deletions, net removal) replacing the label-owned assertion and its raster-parity census machinery with the node-flux recompute, and one docs-only commit adding a plan paragraph and an evidence-archive section. No production module is touched by this node; git diff 0a4b51368..f2dcc15cd --stat confirms exactly the three declared paths.
item_verdicts.done_when: The node's fence asked for a stored parsed record scoring all 5 dimensions, and the underlying node's own done-when (recorded in its manifest) -- the migrated file passing at the worktree tip, the same command passing against a base-revision copy, and a declared negative control failing on the discriminating fixture, each on one fresh all_debug allocation -- was met and I independently reproduced the gate (3 passed) and the negative control (1 failed at the identical index 69, count 1/92).
item_verdicts.goal: Delivered head (commit 2bf422abe on top of base 0a4b51368) replaces the retired label-owned wall-shadow oracle with an independent recompute of the node-flux rule stated by decision wall-node-private-shadow-is-flux-at-the-node: a wall node is private when its own finite flux lies on the private side of the admitted saddle flux and its height sits outside the saddle-bounded band. The diverted fixture's lower private-leg segment is moved inboard (1.58 -> 1.55 at Z -0.46/-0.31) so a wall node's nearest-cell label and its own node-flux verdict now disagree, and the test asserts that disagreement is nonzero.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read at the run directory: 23 keys populated, status complete, two commits, non-empty tests field naming both the gate and base commands with their exit codes, test_logs and negative_control_log naming real on-disk artefacts whose contents I reproduced independently, and evidence_inputs naming the production symbols the fixture depends on. changed_paths (3 entries) matches the actual diff exactly.
item_verdicts.write_paths: All changed paths in both commits sit inside the three declared write paths in the manifest's orientation_write_paths / changed_paths; no concurrent node's path or any other plan is touched; git status --porcelain at the reviewed head is clean.

justifications.durability: The negative control is a real, committed mutation (not a synthetic assertion) that restores the exact retired predicate and is proved to fail on a fixture engineered to discriminate the two rules -- I reproduced the failure myself at the identical index. The test's own disagreeing['single_null'] > 0 assertion additionally guards the fixture itself: if a future edit made the two rules agree again on this fixture, that line -- not just the parity assertion -- would catch it. One narrowing: the test's local _band_limits recomputes the height band from a single admitted saddle (topology.x_point) using lower=upper=saddle_height, while production's x_point_height_limits takes min/max over the full admitted X-candidate set for multi-saddle configurations (topology.py:52-66); the two fixtures here (limited: zero saddles, single_null: one saddle) never exercise that divergence, so this oracle would not by itself catch a regression in the min/max-over-set logic. That logic is exercised elsewhere (tests/test_wall_node_private_shadow.py::test_private_height_bands_exclude_axis_interval_and_require_a_saddle, two saddles at Z=-1/+1), so this is a scope observation about this one oracle rather than a suite-wide coverage gap.
justifications.evidence: Every load-bearing claim in the manifest was independently reproduced rather than read. I reran tests/test_plasma_cell_shadow_telemetry.py at the worktree HEAD (JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, the shared root venv): 3 passed in 128.06s locally (the recorded gate used a fresh all_debug allocation, job 1276266, at 63.52s -- the wall-clock difference is expected between a shared login-node CPU run and a dedicated allocation and does not change the verdict). I also reran the committed negative_control_test.py, which restores the retired label-owned assertion on the discriminating fixture: it failed with the exact reported shape -- 'Mismatched elements: 1 / 92 (1.09%)', mismatch at index [69]: True (ACTUAL) vs False (DESIRED), 1 failed in 91.76s locally against the recorded 33.08s on the allocation -- an identical index and count is strong confirmation the fixture and rule are what the manifest claims. driver.sh, gate.log, base.log and negative_control.log on disk corroborate the base-revision comparison (3 passed 86.48s at 0a4b51368) and the negative-control log's first line repeats the declared control string verbatim, satisfying the node's own contract. The evidence archive section (commit f2dcc15cd) restates every number identically to the logs and to my reproduction. No claim in the manifest could not be verified.
justifications.fit: Mechanism-named helpers throughout (_band_limits, _node_flux_private_mask, test_carrier_private_wall_follows_the_node_flux_rule) with no plan, sprint, ticket, or version label in any symbol, filename, or comment; the commit message and evidence prose describe the mechanism (node flux against the admitted saddle, height band) rather than citing a work item. The diff is a clean replacement -- 135 deletions against 68 insertions -- of the retired-rule oracle with no dead code left behind (the old _inside_boundary helper and the raster-parity census machinery it supported are removed along with the assertions that used them). The negative-control script and driver follow the repository's one-job, on-disk-log idiom.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The migrated oracle implements the accepted decision exactly: test_carrier_private_wall_follows_the_node_flux_rule recomputes the private flag from the wall node's own flux against the admitted saddle flux by polarity and its height against the saddle-bounded band, with cell labels retired from the decision path, and asserts the production carrier read (operator._carrier_shadow_read) against this independent recompute rather than against a fixture-owned constant. The diverted fixture's lower private leg is moved from (1.58, ...) to (1.55, ...) so a wall node's nearest cell centre now reads the opposite flag from its own flux, and the test asserts disagreeing['single_null'] > 0, forcing the fixture to discriminate the retired rule rather than merely agree with both. This directly repairs the finding from the prior review (r-20260922T211725263915) that the file was 'a green oracle for a retired rule' because its two fixtures happened to agree under both rules.
justifications.scope_discipline: Two commits, three changed paths total (tests/test_plasma_cell_shadow_telemetry.py, docs/plans/plasma-cell-read-fidelity.html, docs/evidence/archive/plasma-cell-read-fidelity-landed.html), all inside the three declared write paths with no deletions outside the migrated test file. git diff over the full commit range shows no other module, plan, or sprint state touched; git status at the reviewed head is clean. The scratch artefacts (driver.sh, base_test_copy.py, negative_control_test.py, probe*.py, logs) live entirely under the reports directory, outside the repository.
